doc.title: Zutty Singleton and Marge Singleton Interview, 1969-02-08

chapter: Marge Singleton's St. Louis memories of Jelly Roll
title: The Hawkins brothers' saloon and Nickelodeon
summary: Marge describes the Hawkins brothers' saloon and the Nickelodeon next door, and Mrs. Eubanks, their sister, who sold tickets. Jelly was very young.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And Lowe was walked in the door, stooped over all that money. He was very young. Jelly was very young. My brother was very young.
Lowe was very young. They owned a saloon. And on the other side was the Nickelodeon. And the kid's mother that I went to school with, Mrs. Eubanks, was their sister. Was the Hawkins brother's sister.
She sold tickets at the movie. And they just gave Jelly this. And they just gave Jelly this.
Jabba just came to keep doing it.
And he didn't want to eat money.

And he wasn't dressed up. He wasn't shocked then. I remember his relationship. But he gambled a lot. My brother gambled a lot. The Hawkins brothers gambled a lot. And I learned a whole lot. They had a nephew named Frank. Frank, yeah. He read. And they had a lot of piano in their saloon. They never doubt this. So all came to the other direction of us. Frank, he read. He read. He read.
